name: TRIPOLI
description: Tripoli (Tripoley) is a multi-phase card game combining Pay Cards, Poker, and a Michigan Rummy (Stops) phase. Players ante chips onto a board with labeled sections. Holders of specific Heart cards collect from those sections. Then a Poker round is played, followed by a Stops/Shedding phase. Descended from the 500-year-old German game Poch.

content.text: Tripoli (Tripoley) is a multi-phase card game combining Pay Cards, Poker, and a Michigan Rummy (Stops) phase. Players ante chips onto a board with labeled sections. Holders of specific Heart cards collect from those sections. Then a Poker round is played, followed by a Stops/Shedding phase. Descended from the 500-year-old German game Poch.

Tripoli (also known as Three in One) is a modern North American adaptation of the ancient European game Poch (Pochspiel), which has been played in Germany for at least 500 years. Poch is documented in 15th-century sources; Thierry Depaulis's article in The Playing-Card details its early history. Tripoli retains Poch's three-phase structure (pay cards, betting, Stops) but uses a standard 52-card deck and fixed heart-suit layout; it is sold in North America as Tripoley, Rummoli, Michigan Rummy, and Royal Rummy, and in Australia as Calliente.
Standard 52-card deck. Board/mat with labeled sections.
Deal all cards (one hand is 'dead'). Ante chips to board.

items.text: Rummoli style (collect in Michigan): Omit stage one; layout stakes are collected by anyone who plays the relevant card during the Michigan stage (e.g. play king and queen of hearts consecutively for king-queen stake; play 8-9-10 in one suit consecutively for that stake).
Bid for pay suit: Players bid for the right to choose the pay suit; high bidder adds the bid to the kitty and chooses the suit. Stakes on pay cards are collected during the Michigan stage.
